title: Every way an execution ends is recorded with its cause and recovered by its path: resumed at once, handed off, waited out or final, never by discarding the work
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/supervise.rs, the module comment, `decide` (`RESUME_ATTEMPTS`, `BACKOFF_MS`, the handoff), `revive`, `keep_alive` and `keep_residents`; in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch/worker.rs `decide_worker` and `resume_lost` (a worker is resumed only when its execution was `lost`, once; `resumed_young`), and the ladder in dispatch.rs's module comment; `LIVENESS_FACTS` in crates/spawn-postgres/src/sessions.rs and `died_young!` in crates/spawn-postgres/src/lib.rs; in crates/spawn-core/src/event.rs `EndCause` (`exited`, `stopped`, `lost`) and `ExecutionEnded`; in crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs the module comment, how an execution's end is found and made (`exit_status`, the `is_alive` check, `end`, the final checkpoint, `recover`, `catch_up`) and `claude_settings` (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL when SPAWN_MODEL_RELAY is set); crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/engine.rs (`run`: an engine killed by a signal leaves an empty exit file, which the Bridge records `exited` with no exit code); `claude_line` in crates/spawn-core/src/ingest.rs (an `isApiErrorMessage` line becomes `turn.failed`, its `error` and `apiErrorStatus` dropped) and `ended_execution` in crates/spawn-core/src/observe/classify.rs; `resident_loop` in crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs (`MAX_FAILURES`, `backoff`: ten failed passes in a row end the loop); crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs (`Monitor`, `CHECK_EVERY`, `below_floor`, `hold_new_executions`); `spawn_host_record` and `spawn_control_record` in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; deploy/systemd/spawn-loop.service (Restart=always, RestartSec=5, RestartSteps=5, RestartMaxDelaySec=60; you may not edit it); objective 026 on main (rsi/backlog/026.json: a budget overrun's Stop and its continuation); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 and §3.1 (the liveness rule's table of threats) and docs/design.md §14.

The problem. Spawn's core is one agent that runs forever (the owner's direction, 2026-11-06): the fleet is a client of it. Whether an agent comes back after its execution ends depends today on who keeps it and how it ended, and nothing records why. The Bridge records three end causes: `exited` (from the runner's exit file; an engine killed by a signal leaves the file empty, so a SIGKILL reads `exited` with exit_code null), `stopped` and `lost`. supervise.rs's liveness rule (the supervisor and the residents) resumes every end that was not a stop, at once, then after 20, 40 and 80 s, and after three failed resumes starts a new native session with a handoff summary; it records no cause and treats a killed engine, an exit, a full disk and a host restart alike. The dispatcher resumes an ephemeral worker only when its execution was `lost`, and only once: a worker whose engine was killed, exited or failed on a full disk stays down with its task delivered and unfinished, and only an escalation to the supervisor says so. A model API that is overloaded (529) or rate limited (429), an expired login (401) and an exhausted context end no execution at all: Claude Code writes its API error line to the transcript and waits at its prompt, and nothing retries (without a judge nothing types; with Jev, only the guarded `continue` nudge, three an hour, which neither waits for the cause to clear nor starts a fresh context). Claude Code's transcripts on this host hold such lines: about 54 `API Error: Request rejected (429) · upstream account quota usage limit has been reached` (49 of them name when an account is available again, `... available again at 22:00 UTC`), 21 `API Error: 503 ... no eligible upstream account is currently available`, 8 `API Error: Connection lost mid-response`, 3 `Not logged in · Please run /login` and 2 `Please run /login · API Error: 403 Request not allowed`; Claude Code 2.1.318 tags each line with `error` (authentication_failed, rate_limit, overloaded, server_error, invalid_request, ...) and `apiErrorStatus`, and an exhausted context with the text `Prompt is too long`. A database outage ends the loop itself: ten failed passes in a row, about 22.5 s at the 500 ms interval, and `spawn loop` exits, so the fleet comes back only if systemd starts it again, 5 s later at first and up to 60 s later as RestartSteps grows the delay. The owner chose local hot recovery: every way an execution ends must be classified, and each class must have a defined way back that never throws the work away.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. One record per interruption. An interruption is an execution's end, a turn that failed with a model cause or an exhausted context while its engine stays at its prompt (that is how Claude Code fails a turn), or an outage of Spawn's database that a running execution lived through. The loop records each once, as a control record written by the owner (extend `spawn_host_record`, or add an owner-only record function beside it): `{"type": "execution.interrupted", "agent_id", "session_id", "execution_id", "cause", "evidence", "path", "attempt", "due_ms"}`. `attempt` is the how-manieth interruption of that execution this is (1 for its first), so `recover-<execution id>-<attempt>` names this interruption and no other; `due_ms` is when its revival is due (null on the final path). The record is idempotent: a restarted loop finds it in the log and neither records it again nor revives it twice.
2. The cause, one of exactly these, told from recorded facts: `exited` (the engine exited by itself with code 0; evidence `exit_code`); `crashed` (a non-zero exit code or a signal, or a terminal that disappeared while its terminal server lives on; evidence `exit_code` or `signal`: the runner records the signal that killed the engine, e.g. 9 for SIGKILL, instead of an empty file); `memory_limit` (the engine's resource envelope killed it, objective 029; evidence `scope`, `memory_max`, `oom_kills`); `context_exhausted` (an API error line whose text holds `Prompt is too long`; evidence `event_id` of the turn.failed, `text`); `model_unavailable` (an API error line with status 529, 503, 500, 429 or none, or error overloaded, rate_limit or server_error; evidence `event_id`, `status`, `error`, `text`, and `retry_at_ms` when the text names a time an account is available again); `model_auth` (status 401 or 403, or error authentication_failed, or a text holding `/login`; evidence `event_id`, `status`, `error`, `text`, `credentials`: `path`, `mtime_ms`, `size` of the credentials file as read then); `host_restart` (the end was found by a loop started after it, and the execution's terminal server is gone, so every execution in it ended; evidence `terminal_server` "gone", `loop_started_at_ms`, `boot_id` (/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id) and the one the earlier loop recorded when it did); `database_unavailable` (two or more passes in a row of the loop could not reach its database while the execution ran; evidence `from_ms`, `to_ms` (the loop's clock: the first failed pass and the first good one), `failed_passes`, `error` (one line); an execution that ended inside the outage also names its own `exit_code` or `signal`); `disk_full` (the engine ended while a reading of its workspace's filesystem, taken at the end, was under SPAWN_DISK_FLOOR_GB; evidence `path`, `free_bytes`, `floor_bytes`, `read_at_ms`, `exit_code`); `budget` (the integrator's Stop of a task over its budget, objective 026; evidence the overrun record's event id and the budget); `stopped` (a Stop or Discard from a person or the supervisor, a cancelled task's Stop, or a retirement; evidence `command_id`, `principal`, and `retired` or `task_cancelled` when so). When several hold, the first in this order wins: stopped, budget, memory_limit, host_restart, disk_full, database_unavailable, model_auth, model_unavailable, context_exhausted, crashed, exited. A Stop that is part of a revival (a handoff's) is not an interruption of its own.
3. The path, by cause:
- `resume` (exited, crashed, memory_limit, host_restart): resume the same native session. The first resume of a run is due at once; the k-th resume in a row of a session after SPAWN_RECOVER_BACKOFF_SECS (new, default 10) x 2^(k-1) seconds, at most 64 times the base (today's supervise.rs schedule: at once, 20, 40, 80 s, capped at 640 s). A resume fails when its execution ends again within 60 s of its start before it made progress (no tool call completed and no turn ended after it started); a revival that made progress succeeded, whatever ends it later (today's `died_young` counts every end within 60 s that is lost or has a non-zero exit, progress or not: in objective 032's soak a resident that had worked for 20 s after a revival was killed and backed off 20 s more); the fourth interruption after three failed resumes in a row takes the handoff path instead (today's RESUME_ATTEMPTS), its evidence naming `resumes_failed` 3.
- `handoff` (context_exhausted; budget, by objective 026's continuation): stop the execution if it is still running (its Stop's final checkpoint, as today), then start a new native session in the same Spawn session, the same workspace and branch, due at once. Its prompt is the task's brief (or the resident's role, or the supervisor's charter and today's handoff summary), the interruption (cause, evidence) and the branch head, and says the work is in the workspace to continue, not to redo.
- `wait` (model_unavailable, model_auth, database_unavailable, disk_full): no revival while the cause holds; when it clears, the loop records `{"type": "execution.cleared", "execution_id", "session_id", "cause", "evidence", "waited_ms"}` (evidence: what showed it cleared; waited_ms from the first interruption of the wait), then revives the agent in its own native session: an `input` into the live engine that names the interruption, or a resume if the execution ended. A wait never counts toward the handoff. How each clears: model_unavailable, by retries: the j-th failed turn in a row is retried after SPAWN_RECOVER_MODEL_BACKOFF_SECS (new, default 60) x 2^(j-1) seconds, at most 4 times that base (4 minutes by default: a failed retry costs one refused request, and the cap bounds the time to resume once the API is back), or at `retry_at_ms` when that is later; a retry whose turn fails again with a model cause is the next interruption of the same execution (a new record, `attempt` + 1); the wait is cleared when a retried turn gets a model answer (a tool call or an assistant line that is no API error): for model_unavailable the retry is the revival, so its `execution.cleared` comes after it, at that answer (Spawn holds no model credentials to probe with). model_auth: no retry while the credentials file ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json, else $HOME/.claude/.credentials.json, as the loop's own environment names it) keeps its modification time and size, read every SPAWN_RECOVER_PROBE_SECS (new, default 10); cleared when it changes; one retry every SPAWN_RECOVER_AUTH_RETRY_SECS (new, default 1800) while it does not. database_unavailable: cleared at the loop's first pass that reaches the database; an execution that ran through the outage needs no revival (its cleared record names the catch-up checkpoint, the commit holding what it wrote meanwhile); one that ended inside it is resumed. disk_full: cleared at a reading of the workspace's filesystem at or above SPAWN_DISK_FLOOR_GB, taken every SPAWN_RECOVER_PROBE_SECS while the wait is open.
- `final` (stopped): never revived by Spawn.
4. The revival is one command whose idempotency key is `recover-<execution id>-<attempt>` (the interruption it answers): `resume` for the resume path and a wait whose execution ended, `start` for a handoff, `input` for a wait whose engine is still at its prompt. It is submitted no earlier than `due_ms`; its outcome is read back from the command queue (§14) and a failed one counts as a failed resume.
5. No path discards the workspace or the checkpointed work: an ending execution's final checkpoint is taken as today; a handoff stops first and starts on the same branch; a wait leaves the engine or its workspace as it is; a final path keeps the branch. Work lost is 0 lines.
6. The loop outlives a database outage. A pass that failed only because the database could not be reached does not count toward MAX_FAILURES: the loop keeps passing on its backoff (at most 30 intervals), the engines run on untouched, and it records the outage's interruptions at its first good pass, then checkpoints what the engines wrote meanwhile. Every other failure counts as today.
7. One rule for every agent: the supervisor, the residents and the ephemeral workers (a worker with a delivered task that is not reported or cancelled; an idle worker with no open task is not revived). supervise.rs's `decide` and the dispatcher's `resume_lost` give way to it; supervise.rs keeps the charter and the handoff summary. Under the disk floor no new execution starts (as today); the supervisor is still kept, so someone can act.
8. Causality (§14): a cause is read from recorded facts (the end's exit status or signal, the transcript's API error line by its event id, the command that stopped it, the loop's measured passes, a free-space reading with its time, the terminal server's state at recovery), each named in the evidence; a revival names the interruption it answers by its key and waits for its `due_ms`; a wait clears on a recorded observation (a model answer, a changed credentials file, a good pass, a reading), never on time alone; a restarted loop decides from the log what was recorded and sent.

How the saving shows, in numbers. Uptime of a faulted worker: today it is 0 for good after six of the nine fault kinds the scenario injects (crashed, exited, context_exhausted, model_unavailable, model_auth, disk_full; measures below). Required: every one comes back, the resume paths within 20 s of the end (today 2.8-3.0 s for a resident and 2.6-4.2 s after a host restart's loop start, where Spawn resumes at all), a handoff within 30 s, a wait within 12-15 s of its cause clearing (the backoff and the probe); the loop never exits for a database outage (today it exits 22.7-22.9 s into one and comes back only by systemd's restart); every interruption recorded within 5 s; work lost 0 lines (as today wherever an agent came back). Objective 032 (the soak) measures the same numbers over a long run. On 017's scorecard: autonomy and reliability higher (no person resumes a downed worker), cost lower (no task redone because its worker never came back); no other objective's scenario may regress.

State the rule in supervise.rs's and dispatch.rs's module comments, in bridge.rs's module comment (the end's cause and the signal), in docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 and §3.1 (the table of threats: each cause, its path, its numbers) and in schema.sql beside the record function. Add unit tests: the classification of each cause from its facts and the precedence when several hold (a signal is crashed, exit 0 is exited, a non-zero exit under the disk floor is disk_full, a Stop by a person is stopped, a 529, 503, 429 and a connection error are model_unavailable, 401, 403 and `/login` are model_auth, `Prompt is too long` is context_exhausted, an end found at recovery with its terminal server gone is host_restart, an end inside a database outage is database_unavailable); a 429 text that names a time sets `retry_at_ms`; each path's decision as a pure function of the facts and the time: the first resume at once, then 20, 40, 80 s and the cap, three failed resumes then a handoff, the model backoff doubling to its cap (4 x the base) and waiting for `retry_at_ms`; a resume that ended within 60 s after a tool call is no failed resume, one that ended before any is, no auth retry until the credentials change or the slow retry is due, the disk wait until a reading at the floor, final never revived; `attempt` and the keys unique per execution across a model wait, a database outage and a host restart of the same execution; the runner's signal in the exit file; database failures not counted toward MAX_FAILURES; a restarted loop records nothing twice and revives nothing twice. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: the record function accepts `execution.interrupted` and `execution.cleared` with their fields from the owner only, and refuses an unknown cause or path.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/028.sh (read it: its header lists today's measures). A real `spawn loop` (the Bridge, the dispatcher, the supervisor, no model judge), run as systemd runs spawn-loop.service (started again 5 s after it exits), runs six ephemeral workers of one mission, each with a delivered task, and one resident with a task, on a fake engine: once given work it makes one step a second, a model request to the relay its --settings name with the credentials in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json, then a tool call that appends the next numbered line to work.txt in its workspace; a failed request ends its turn as Claude Code does (the API error line, the engine at its prompt). The scenario's fake relay answers each agent as the scenario sets it (200, 529, 401 unless the new token, 400 "prompt is too long" to one native session); the loop reaches its database through a forwarder the scenario cuts; a `df` first on the loop's PATH fakes the free space. Settings: SPAWN_RECOVER_BACKOFF_SECS=2, SPAWN_RECOVER_MODEL_BACKOFF_SECS=2, SPAWN_RECOVER_AUTH_RETRY_SECS=600, SPAWN_RECOVER_PROBE_SECS=2, SPAWN_DISK_FLOOR_GB=1. It checks, faults (1)-(6) at once on an agent each, then (7)-(9) in turn:
- (1) a worker's engine is killed (SIGKILL): within 5 s of its end an `execution.interrupted`, cause `crashed` (evidence `signal` 9), path `resume`, due at once; within 5 s of it the resume `recover-<execution>-<attempt>`; the engine works again in the same native session within 20 s of the end, its workspace holding every line it wrote;
- (2) a worker's and the resident's engines exit 0 with their tasks unfinished: the same with cause `exited` (evidence `exit_code` 0);
- (3) the model answers a worker's native session "prompt is too long": cause `context_exhausted` (evidence `text`), path `handoff`, the revival a `start`; the engine works in a new native session within 30 s of the failed turn, with every line;
- (4) the model answers a worker 529 for 10 s: cause `model_unavailable` (evidence `status` 529), path `wait`; the j-th failure in a row due no sooner than 2 x 2^(j-1) s (at most 8 s, the cap) after its record and retried by its key no earlier; at most 4 requests in the 10 s; an `execution.cleared`; the same native session works again within 12 s of the model's recovery; no handoff;
- (5) the model answers a worker 401 until the credentials file holds a new token (written 14 s in): cause `model_auth` (evidence `status` 401, `credentials.path`), path `wait`; no revival and at most one more 401 before the change; `execution.cleared` within 6 s of it; the same native session works again within 12 s of it;
- (6) a person stops a worker: cause `stopped` (evidence `command_id` of the Stop), path `final`; no revival; its branch holds every line;
- (7) the loop's database is cut for 30 s: the loop does not exit; no engine ends; each execution that ran through it gets cause `database_unavailable` (evidence `from_ms`, `to_ms`, `failed_passes` 2 or more) and an `execution.cleared`; the outage's work reaches each branch within 15 s of its end;
- (8) the host restarts: the loop is stopped as systemd stops it (SIGTERM, its pass finished), the terminal server is killed with every engine in it, and the loop starts 2 s later: each execution gets cause `host_restart` (evidence `terminal_server` "gone"), path `resume`, its resume by key, and works again in its native session within 20 s of the loop's start, with every line;
- (9) the free space reads 100 MiB under the 1 GiB floor and a worker's engine fails with ENOSPC (exit 1): cause `disk_full` (evidence `free_bytes` under `floor_bytes` 1073741824), path `wait`; no revival in the 15 s the disk stays full; `execution.cleared` within 6 s of room; the same native session works again within 15 s;
- (10) every agent's branch holds its work.txt whole (lines 1..n in order): no work lost.
On the live main (b950e25; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "(1) agent_worker_crash_1's execution exec_1 ended after its engine was killed (SIGKILL) (the Bridge recorded execution.ended exited exit_code=null), and no execution.interrupted names its cause; every end records its cause (crashed) and the path it takes: revivals [none]; its engine never worked again". With BB_028_MEASURE=1 (only to show today's behaviour) it goes on, resuming by hand (as a person would) the agents Spawn left down so that the later faults have agents to fault: the killed worker (recorded `exited`, exit_code null) and the worker that exited 0 are never resumed; the resident that exited 0 is resumed by spawn-liveness 1.0-1.2 s after it was told to exit and works again 2.8-3.0 s after, every line kept; the worker whose context is exhausted, the one refused with 529 (1 request in the 10 s, its failed turn, never retried) and the one refused with 401 (never revived, before or after the renewal) wait at their prompts for good; the stopped worker stays down with every line on its branch (as required); the loop exits 22.7-22.9 s into the 30 s outage ("10 failed passes in a row"), its restart 5 s later fails while the database is still cut and the next, 2.7-2.9 s after the outage, holds, the outage's work on the branches 4.6 s after it (no engine ended); after the host restart every worker is resumed as `lost` by the dispatcher (dispatch-resume-<execution>) and the resident by spawn-liveness, 0.7-0.8 s after the loop's start, working again 2.6-4.2 s after it with every line; the worker that failed with ENOSPC (recorded `exited`, exit_code 1) is never revived; no run recorded an `execution.interrupted` or `execution.cleared`. The plain run fails at (1) in 25-26 s, the measure run takes 160-162 s. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure; on a passing tree it takes about 2-3 minutes.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh and scripts/model-relay.py among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
